subject: Post-demo: model fit validation, schema hardening & toolcall plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@novacare.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit validation, schema hardening & toolcall plan

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single plan to share with your security and engineering teams.

Recap (short):
- Use-case: intake extraction + structured claim summaries (JSON output) for downstream billing workflows.
- Key concern: strict JSON schema compliance + SLOs for 95th%-ile latency < 600ms for single-item requests.
- Data sensitivity: PHI tokens in free text; customer prefers private deployment if SOC2 evidence + KMS integration are acceptable.

Recommended evaluation matrix (what we'll run during the pilot):
1) Model candidates: Redwood-v2-medium-q4 (default), Llama-2-13B-q4f16 (fallback), Redwood-v1-7B for low-cost bursts.
2) Benchmarks: attached novacare_benchmarks_20280801.csv — includes latency, token cost, structured-output success rate (schema pass %).
3) Prompt set: attached novacare_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (200 representative examples from your QA team).
4) Structured-output validation: run the JSON schema tests (examples attached: schema_examples_v2.json) with a strict 'schema-first' check and a permissive 'repair & retry' path.

Tool/function calling plan:
- We'll validate two modes: 1) function-calling (explicit output fields) and 2) constrained JSON responses with schema enforcement in the harness.
- Retries: exponential backoff, 3 attempts, capture idempotency key so downstream dedup is safe. If schema still fails on last retry, fallback to a compact text failure mode (human-in-the-loop ticket).

Security/compliance asks from your side (we'll gather):
- SOC2 Type II report or AICPA bridge letter (we can provide Redwood's SOC2 report and an architecture note).
- KMS integration details for the pilot.

Proposed next steps (action items):
- From Redwood (sean): schedule a 1-week canary run using the 200-example prompt set, include JSON schema checks and toolcall traces. (ETA: Aug 8 start)
- From Novacare (alex): share any additional edge-case prompts + confirm ops+security contact for evidence review.
- Mutually agree on success criteria: schema pass rate >= 98% and monitoring alerts for regression > 2% in any day.

Attachments: novacare_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), novacare_benchmarks_20280801.csv (baseline runs), schema_examples_v2.json (schemas + example repairs)

If that looks good I'll lock in the canary start and loop in Marissa (eval lead) and Laura (SRE/ops).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Thanks Sean — useful summary. A couple clarifying Qs from ops/security before we confirm the pilot schedule: 

1) On retries: does the retry path preserve the original prompt and idempotency key? We need deterministic behavior so our billing pipeline doesn't dedupe incorrectly.
2) Schema failures: what constitutes a 'repair' attempt vs a failure that gets human ticketed? Are repairs recorded in audit logs?
3) Can you share the SOC2 artifacts and a short note on where keys live when running Dedicated vs Private?

Also cc'ing our security lead (ops+security) so they can surface any additional evidence requests.

Would appreciate a short answer doc we can attach to our procurement notes.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit validation, schema hardening & toolcall plan

Alex — short answers inline, happy to expand in a one-pager: 

1) Retries and idempotency: yes — our client SDK attaches a request_id and idempotency_key by default. Retries re-use the same idempotency_key for the logical request; we log each attempt in the request trace. That ensures downstream billing keys are not duplicated.

2) Repair vs failure: repair attempts are deterministic transformations we run server-side in the harness: e.g. sanitize trailing commas, coerce date formats, and enforce required keys with null placeholders. We record a 'repair' flag per-response in the audit log and keep both original and repaired outputs (audit retention is part of the pilot config). If repairs fail (schema still invalid after N=1 repair + 3 retries), we mark as 'schema_exception' and open a ticket to the configured Slack channel / human queue.

3) SOC2 & key location: attaching the SOC2 summary (we'll send the full report under NDA). For Dedicated: keys can be customer-managed via KMS; for Private on-prem we support HSM integration. I'll loop Laura for the architecture note.

Technical plan (what Redwood will run in the canary):
- 1,000 requests/day for 7 days for across the three model candidates above (we'll ramp).
- For each request we capture: model, tokens in/out, latency, schema_pass (bool), repair_applied (bool), retry_count.
- Early-stop rule: if schema_pass < 95% for any model at day-3 we pause and analyze.

Attachments included in this email: novacare_benchmarks_20280801.csv (baseline), schema_examples_v2.json

I'll prepare the brief answers doc and a small architecture slide for ops. Proposed canary start remains Aug 8 — is that ok on your end?

Best,
Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding a few notes from the eval perspective before we share the one-pager externally: 

- Evaluation metrics: primary = schema_pass_rate; secondary = BLEU-like string match for key fields, and fuzzy-match on extracted entities (use token-level edit distance). We should surface per-field pass rates so Novacare can see which fields are brittle (dates, ICD codes).
- Prompt set: I'll augment the provided 200 examples with 60 synthetic edge-cases (truncated notes, OCR artifacts, mixed-language snippets) — will attach novacare_prompt_set_v1_augmented.jsonl to the Drive link.
- Toolcall traces: capture the function-call payloads (schema + parameters) and include an option to strip PHI before they land in Redwood's retained traces — will make sure retention settings are configurable at run start.

I'll also paste a short test harness snippet below that the engineering team can run locally to reproduce failures.

> snippet: eval-harness run --prompts novacare_prompt_set_v1.jsonl --schema schema_examples_v2.json --models redwood-v2-medium-q4,llama2-13b-q4 --record-traces --repair-policy "sanitize_basic"

Assigning action: Karthik, can you own the SRE/runbook part (rate limits + backoff) and Laura can draft the short architecture note for ops. I'll finish the augmented prompt set by EOD Wed.

-Marissa
